Let

\[
q=2^d,\qquad n=|\mathcal P_d|=|\mathcal H_d|=2^{d+1}-1=2q-1.
\]

Each point is incident with

\[
k=2^d-1=q-1
\]

hyperplanes, and two distinct points lie in

\[
\lambda=2^{d-1}-1
\]

common hyperplanes. Thus the point-hyperplane incidence matrix \(A\) satisfies

\[
AA^T=(k-\lambda)I+\lambda J=2^{d-1}I+(2^{d-1}-1)J.
\]

The graph distances are:

\[
\rho(P,P')=2\quad(P\ne P'),\qquad \rho(H,H')=2\quad(H\ne H'),
\]

and

\[
\rho(P,H)=
\begin{cases}
1,&P\subset H,\\
3,&P\not\subset H.
\end{cases}
\]

So, for \(a=2^p,\ b=3^p\), the cross-block distance matrix is

\[
B=bJ+(1-b)A.
\]

For a coefficient vector \(c=(u,v)\), with \(u\) on points and \(v\) on hyperplanes, impose

\[
\sum u+\sum v=0.
\]

Decompose

\[
u=\alpha \mathbf 1+u_0,\qquad v=-\alpha \mathbf 1+v_0,
\]

where \(u_0,v_0\perp \mathbf 1\). The quadratic form splits into two independent parts.

The constant antisymmetric direction gives the condition

\[
q3^p+(q-1)-2(q-1)2^p\ge 0. \tag{1}
\]

The orthogonal directions give the condition

\[
(3^p-1)2^{(d-1)/2}\le 2^p. \tag{2}
\]

Indeed, on \(\mathbf 1^\perp\), the singular values of \(A\) are all

\[
\sqrt{2^{d-1}},
\]

so the largest relevant eigenvalue is

\[
-2^p+(3^p-1)2^{(d-1)/2}.
\]

For \(d=2,3,4\), condition (1) never fails before condition (2), so \(\wp_d\) is determined by (2). Then the nullspace at \(p=\wp_d\) has dimension \(n-1>1\).

For \(d\ge 5\), condition (1) fails first. Hence \(\wp_d\) is the first positive root of

\[
q3^p+(q-1)-2(q-1)2^p=0.
\]

At that root only the constant antisymmetric direction is null, namely

\[
c_P=1,\qquad c_H=-1,
\]

up to scalar. Thus

\[
\dim E_d=1\qquad(d\ge5),
\]

and therefore

\[
d_*=5.
\]

It remains to compute the limit. Since \(\wp_d\to0\), expand the root equation at \(p=0\):

\[
q(1+p\log 3)+(q-1)-2(q-1)(1+p\log 2)+O(qp^2)=0.
\]

The constant term is \(1\), and the linear coefficient is

\[
q\log 3-2(q-1)\log 2
=-q\log\frac43+O(1).
\]

Thus

\[
\wp_d\sim \frac{1}{q\log(4/3)}
=\frac{1}{2^d\log(4/3)}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\lim_{d\to\infty}2^d\wp_d=\frac1{\log(4/3)}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(d_*,\ \lim_{d\to\infty}2^d\wp_d\right)
=
\left(5,\ \frac1{\log(4/3)}\right)}
\]
